title: Flying and emotion
titleChinese: 高空飞行对情绪的影响
paragraphs: Have you ever found yourself watching a trashy film on an aeroplane, tears welling up as the cheesy crooner sings its theme song? I certainly have. And I’m not alone. So much so that Virgin Atlantic recently released a list of the films that cause people to cry the most. Get this: 7% of people admitted to crying during the sad parts, while 10% owned up to getting emotional at happy endings. What is it about being 35,000 feet up in the air that causes such heightened emotions?

So, what’s going on? How does air travel tap into our hidden emotions? A study from the Netherlands has shown adults cry due to feelings of separation, loneliness or powerlessness. All of these are easily experienced when flying: you‘re far from family, often alone, and have no control over the aircraft’s flight.

Another theory relates to the lack of distraction. When you‘re strapped into your seat in a sealed cabin in the sky, there’s not a lot you can do. So we are able to invest ourselves more fully into the movies we watch.

Then there‘s the physical space. Air pressure and oxygen levels are lower, and this can affect our mental state. Conditions in an aeroplane resemble those at an altitude of 2,400m. The reduced oxygen at this height can affect the brain. According to a study by the US Institute of Medicine: “the initial mood experienced at altitude is euphoria, followed by depression.”

And what about the movies themselves? Virgin say top culprits include tearjerkers such as Billy Elliot, Eat Pray Love and, at number one position, Toy Story 3. Their emotional firepower even caused the aeroplane to slap tongue-in-cheek “emotional health warnings” on select movies back in 2011.

Virgin Atlantic film critic Jason Solomons said at the time, “On a flight, we‘re isolated, leaving loved ones or aching to be reunited with them. We’re nervous, we‘re tired, we might have had a drink at a time we usually wouldn’t, and if we see an image, a scene that reflects our emotional state, frankly we‘re suckers. Flying and films is a heady cocktail.

vocabulary.entry: well up [phr.] /wel ʌp/ 涌出；涌上心头（指泪水）(书面语)
vocabulary.example: Tears welled up in her eyes when she heard the news.
vocabulary.translation: 听到这个消息时，泪水涌上了她的眼眶。

vocabulary.entry: trashy [adj.] /ˈtræʃi/ 低俗的；蹩脚的；无价值的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She enjoys reading trashy novels on the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢在海滩上读低俗小说。

vocabulary.entry: crooner [n.] /ˈkruːnə/ 低吟歌手；流行歌手
vocabulary.example: The old crooner sang a romantic ballad.
vocabulary.translation: 那位老歌手唱了一首浪漫的情歌。

vocabulary.entry: owned up to [phr.] /əʊnd ʌp tuː/ 承认；坦白 (口语；原形: own up to)
vocabulary.example: He finally owned up to breaking the vase.
vocabulary.translation: 他终于承认打碎了花瓶。

vocabulary.entry: heightened emotions [n. pl.] /ˈhaɪtənd ɪˈməʊʃənz/ 更强烈的情绪；情绪高涨 (书面语；单数: heightened emotion)
vocabulary.example: The movie‘s climax caused heightened emotions in the audience.
vocabulary.translation: 电影的高潮引发了观众强烈的情绪。

vocabulary.entry: tap into [phr.] /tæp ˈɪntə/ 挖掘；利用；触动
vocabulary.example: The advertisement taps into people’s fear of missing out.
vocabulary.translation: 这则广告利用了人们害怕错过的心理。

vocabulary.entry: powerlessness [n.] /ˈpaʊələsnəs/ 无力；无能为力 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The feeling of powerlessness can lead to depression.
vocabulary.translation: 无力感可能导致抑郁。

vocabulary.entry: distraction [n.] /dɪˈstrækʃən/ 分心；使人分心的事物
vocabulary.example: The TV was a distraction from his homework.
vocabulary.translation: 电视是让他做作业时分心的东西。

vocabulary.entry: euphoria [n.] /juːˈfɔːriə/ 兴奋；狂喜；陶醉感 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Winning the championship filled the team with euphoria.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得冠军让整个团队沉浸在狂喜之中。

vocabulary.entry: culprits [n. pl.] /ˈkʌlprɪts/ 原因；起因；罪犯 (单数: culprit)
vocabulary.example: The main culprits of air pollution are cars and factories.
vocabulary.translation: 空气污染的主要原因是汽车和工厂。

vocabulary.entry: tearjerkers [n. pl.] /ˈtɪədʒɜːkəz/ 催人泪下的电影（或书籍等）(口语；单数: tearjerker)
vocabulary.example: Romantic dramas are often tearjerkers.
vocabulary.translation: 浪漫剧情片常常催人泪下。

vocabulary.entry: tongue-in-cheek [adj.] /ˌtʌŋ ɪn ˈtʃiːk/ 半开玩笑的；不认真的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: His comment was tongue-in-cheek, not meant to offend.
vocabulary.translation: 他的评论是半开玩笑的，并非有意冒犯。

vocabulary.entry: be isolated [phr.] /biː ˈaɪsəleɪtɪd/ 被隔离；与世隔绝
vocabulary.example: During the flight, passengers feel isolated from the outside world.
vocabulary.translation: 飞行期间，乘客感觉与外界隔绝。

vocabulary.entry: ache to [phr.] /eɪk tuː/ 渴望；热望 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: She ached to see her family again.
vocabulary.translation: 她渴望再次见到家人。

vocabulary.entry: suckers [n. pl.] /ˈsʌkəz/ 容易上当的人；轻信的人 (口语；单数: sucker)
vocabulary.example: Scammers target suckers who believe their lies.
vocabulary.translation: 骗子瞄准那些相信他们谎言的易骗之人。

vocabulary.entry: a heady cocktail [phr.] /ə ˈhedi ˈkɒkteɪl/ 令人陶醉的混合物；令人兴奋的组合 (比喻)
vocabulary.example: The combination of love and danger was a heady cocktail.
vocabulary.translation: 爱与危险的结合是一种令人陶醉的混合物。

vocabulary.entry: get this [phr.] /ɡet ðɪs/ 听着；你听听这个（用于引起注意）(口语)
vocabulary.example: Get this – he won the lottery twice!
vocabulary.translation: 你听听这个——他中了两次彩票！

vocabulary.entry: carry out [phr.] /ˈkæri aʊt/ 实施；执行；进行
vocabulary.example: The experiment was carried out successfully.
vocabulary.translation: 实验成功进行。

vocabulary.entry: be likely to [phr.] /biː ˈlaɪkli tuː/ 可能；有可能
vocabulary.example: It is likely to rain later today.
vocabulary.translation: 今天晚些时候可能会下雨。

vocabulary.entry: in all [phr.] /ɪn ɔːl/ 总共；合计
vocabulary.example: There were fifty people in all at the party.
vocabulary.translation: 派对上总共有五十人。

sentences.chinese: 你有没有发现自己在飞机上看一部蹩脚电影时，随着蹩脚的流行歌手演唱主题曲而热泪盈眶？

sentences.chinese: 我当然有过。

sentences.english: And I’m not alone.
sentences.chinese: 而且不止我一个人这样。

sentences.chinese: 以至于维珍大西洋航空公司最近发布了一份最让人落泪的电影名单。

sentences.chinese: 听听这个：7%的人承认在悲伤情节时哭过，而10%的人承认在幸福结局时情绪激动。

sentences.english: What is it about being 35,000 feet up in the air that causes such heightened emotions?
sentences.chinese: 在35000英尺的高空，是什么导致了如此强烈的情绪呢？

sentences.english: So, what’s going on?
sentences.chinese: 那么，这是怎么回事呢？

sentences.english: How does air travel tap into our hidden emotions?
sentences.chinese: 乘坐飞机旅行是如何触动我们隐藏的情感的呢？

sentences.english: A study from the Netherlands has shown adults cry due to feelings of separation, loneliness or powerlessness.
sentences.chinese: 荷兰的一项研究表明，成年人会因为分离、孤独或无力感而哭泣。

sentences.english: All of these are easily experienced when flying: you‘re far from family, often alone, and have no control over the aircraft’s flight.
sentences.chinese: 在飞行时，这些感受都很容易体会到：你远离家人，常常独自一人，而且无法控制飞机的飞行。

sentences.english: Another theory relates to the lack of distraction.
sentences.chinese: 另一种理论与缺乏分散注意力的事物有关。

sentences.english: When you‘re strapped into your seat in a sealed cabin in the sky, there’s not a lot you can do.
sentences.chinese: 当你被捆绑在天空中一个密封的客舱里的座位上时，你能做的事情并不多。

sentences.english: So we are able to invest ourselves more fully into the movies we watch.
sentences.chinese: 所以我们能够更全身心地投入到我们所看的电影中。

sentences.english: Then there‘s the physical space.
sentences.chinese: 然后是物理空间的因素。

sentences.english: Air pressure and oxygen levels are lower, and this can affect our mental state.
sentences.chinese: 气压和氧气含量较低，这会影响我们的精神状态。

sentences.english: Conditions in an aeroplane resemble those at an altitude of 2,400m.
sentences.chinese: 飞机内的环境类似于海拔2400米处的环境。

sentences.english: The reduced oxygen at this height can affect the brain.
sentences.chinese: 在这个高度氧气含量的降低会影响大脑。

sentences.english: According to a study by the US Institute of Medicine: “the initial mood experienced at altitude is euphoria, followed by depression.”
sentences.chinese: 根据美国医学研究所的一项研究：“在高海拔地区最初的情绪体验是兴奋，随后是抑郁。”

sentences.english: And what about the movies themselves?
sentences.chinese: 那么电影本身呢？

sentences.chinese: 维珍航空公司表示，最让人落泪的电影包括《跳出我天地》、《美食、祈祷和恋爱》，排名第一的是《玩具总动员3》。

sentences.english: Their emotional firepower even caused the aeroplane to slap tongue-in-cheek “emotional health warnings” on select movies back in 2011.
sentences.chinese: 这些电影的情感冲击力甚至使得航空公司在2011年对某些电影半开玩笑似的贴上了“情感健康警告”。

sentences.chinese: 维珍大西洋航空公司的影评人杰森·所罗门斯当时说：“在飞行途中，我们与世隔绝，离开了所爱的人，或者渴望与他们团聚。

sentences.chinese: 我们紧张、疲惫，我们可能会在平时不会喝酒的时候喝上一杯，如果我们看到一个画面、一个反映我们情感状态的场景，坦率地说，我们就变成容易被骗的傻瓜。

sentences.english: Flying and films is a heady cocktail.
sentences.chinese: 坐飞机看电影就像喝了一杯令人陶醉的鸡尾酒。”
